fair_value_reason: NTM EPS in Sept 2027 of ~$12.0 (FY28 consensus $11.74 rolled forward a quarter) x ~26x (the middle of the agents' 25.5-28x range, consistent with a partial repeat of the 2024-style de-rate) = ~$312. FCF cross-check: ~$14.9B NTM net income x ~92% conversion at a 3.5-3.6% yield, plus ~$1-3/share net cash (actual net cash today is $1.46B, not the ~$6B agent_1 projects) = ~$305-315. The agent mean is $311.6, so this is not a change; it is 4% below spot and within noise.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 converged: all five now use the $9.51/$11.74 FY27/FY28 consensus and SEMI's +22%/+14% WFE path, and fair values sit in a tight $302-321 band against a $324.48 spot. The only remaining disagreement is the Sept-2027 multiple (25.5-28x NTM), and history says semicap de-rates after multiple peaks (Lam's year-end P/E fell 27-57% in 2018, 2022 and 2024). But Lam has already de-rated from ~46x to ~34x FY27 since the June high, and peers trade at similar multiples. There is no edge: fair value (~$312) is ~4% below spot, a fraction of one year's ~50% volatility, so the ladder is essentially a coin flip at spot (P = 0.49) with a right skew. Treat it as a small, high-beta satellite and expect large swings around the late-October report.
key_drivers: Forward multiple: 34x FY27 / 27.6x FY28 today, down from ~46x FY27 at the June 30 high. The base case assumes ~26x NTM in Sept 2027; Lam's multiple fell 27-57% in the year after each of the last three multiple peaks (2018, 2022, 2024).
Earnings base: FY27 $9.51 / FY28 $11.74 consensus (S&P Global). The Sep-quarter guide is $8.1B / $2.15, and trailing P/E is ~56x on FY26 EPS of $5.79.

Industry: SEMI (Jul 2026) sees WFE +21.8% in 2027 (~$175B) and +14.1% in 2028. TSMC 2027 capex estimates run up to $85B, Micron FY27 capex is above the mid-$40Bs, and memory contract prices are rising 10-20% QoQ in 4Q26.
Sentiment and vol: realized vol is 55-73%, beta 1.86. The Sep 14 AI 'pacing' call cut the stock 18% in three days before it fully retraced.
China is 26% of revenue (from 43%); the MATCH Act was softened in committee and has had no floor vote.
